data.benchmarkNote: W Hospitality Group, Hotel Chain Development Pipelines in Africa 2026 (published 10 March 2026). Africa-wide the pipeline reached a record 123,846 rooms across 675 properties, up 18.6% year on year. Branded chain projects only.

markets.note: Fourth-largest pipeline in Africa and one of the highest construction ratios on the continent — nearly four in five planned rooms are actually being built, not just announced. For an existing Nairobi or Mara operator this is the clearest supply-side warning on the list: this room count is largely committed capital, not speculation.

Eighth in Africa, third-highest construction ratio. Smaller average property size (143 rooms) than Kenya, consistent with a resort and lodge mix rather than big-box city hotels. Zanzibar is absorbing a meaningful share — see the signings below.

Does NOT appear in the W Hospitality top-ten. That is a genuine finding rather than a gap in our data: on chain-pipeline measures Uganda is not attracting branded development at the scale of its neighbours. Individual projects are still landing (Hilton Kampala, Kampala Marriott — below), but an owner in Kampala faces materially less incoming branded supply than one in Nairobi.
markets.source: W Hospitality Group / FHS Africa 2026 (absence from top-10)

markets.note: Also absent from the W Hospitality top-ten, yet running one of the region's most active luxury signing programmes (LUX*, SLH, Aleph — below). The contradiction is the point: Rwanda's growth is small-format and high-rate, which does not register in a room-count league table but does compete directly for the premium guest.
markets.source: W Hospitality Group / FHS Africa 2026 (absence from top-10)

markets.note: NOT one of our five home markets — tracked as a COMPARATOR because Addis Ababa and Ethiopian Airlines move East African demand. Ethiopia holds the HIGHEST construction ratio on the continent (79.9% of 5,964 pipeline rooms across 34 hotels actually being built), fifth-largest African pipeline. Much of it is timed to COP32 in Addis Ababa in 2027, expected to draw 80,000+ international delegates. Read-across for EA owners: Addis is Ethiopian Airlines’ hub and the connecting gateway for a large share of long-haul arrivals into Nairobi, Kigali, Entebbe, Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar — a supply-and-airlift surge there is a feeder-capacity and city-MICE signal for the whole region, not a distant story.
markets.source: W Hospitality Group, Hotel Chain Development Pipelines in Africa 2026 (10 Mar 2026), via ENA / Capital Ethiopia / ATTA; under-construction figure corrected 4,765 to 4,768 on 9 Nov 2026 per the FHS Africa / W Hospitality release (APO Group via Hospitality Net and africa.com, 10 Mar 2026)

projects.property: Mereshi Safari Camp, Serengeti, Autograph Collection
projects.detail: ADDED 5 NOV 2026. 18 elevated tented suites of 95m2 each on 55 acres near the Fort Ikoma Gate, Robanda, western Serengeti. Owner Delaware Investments; designed by Dunia Design, as was sister property Mapito Safari Camp. About 95% of materials and furnishings sourced in Tanzania; about 100 permanent jobs, over 90% held by Tanzanians. NOTE: our 4 Nov Evening Wrap described this as an opening dated 12 Oct; 12 Oct is the date of the announcement, and the camp is ANTICIPATED to open in November. We have not confirmed it has opened. 9 NOV 2026 CHECK: owner Delaware Investments' own project page still lists Mereshi as 'In Development', opening 'Nov '26' (read 9 Nov 2026); no opening release from Marriott or the owner found. The date has slipped once already: Marriott's own signing release (29 Apr 2025, via Hospitality Net) anticipated a Q3 2025 opening with 16 tented suites including a two-bedroom villa, against 18 suites in the owner's Oct 2026 release. Single-source, not verified by us: The Points Guy (21 Oct 2026, modified 29 Oct) reports Marriott.com taking bookings only for stays from 4 January 2027.
projects.impact: Another Marriott-flagged camp in the western Serengeti puts Bonvoy points and US distribution next to independent Ikoma and Grumeti camps. Expect it in 2027 agent rate comparisons.
projects.source: Delaware Investments via Hospitality Net, 12 Oct 2026 (updated 19 Oct); Delaware Investments project page, read 9 Nov 2026; Marriott International release via Hospitality Net, 29 Apr 2025

projects.property: Kitirua Plains Lodge, an A&K Sanctuary
projects.detail: ADDED 9 NOV 2026. 13 suites (eleven one-bedroom, two two-bedroom) on a 128-acre private concession bordering Amboseli National Park, facing Kilimanjaro. A&K had targeted 1 June 2026; Sanctuary Retreats posted 'Kitirua Plains Lodge, an A&K Sanctuary is Now Open' on 2 June 2026, and an A&K release reproduced by Le Journal des Palaces is dated 10 July 2026 and says the lodge is 'now open and accepting reservations'. A Tourism Update item of 29 Oct 2026 reported it open, but it has been trading since mid-2026. A&K's own site did not render for us.
projects.impact: Another top-tier branded lodge in Amboseli, a park dominated by mid-market lodges and a few high-end conservancy camps. With only 13 suites it does not shift supply, but A&K's own tour volume feeds it directly. Expect it to set a new rate ceiling for Amboseli.
projects.source: Sanctuary Retreats member notice on ATTA, 2 Jun 2026 (atta.travel/resource/kitirua-plains-lodge--an-a-k-sanctuary-is-now-open.html); A&K release via Le Journal des Palaces, 10 Jul 2026 (pressrelease-78878)

projects.detail: Six private riverside villas with plunge pools on the Great Ruaha River in Ruaha National Park (Iringa region); access by Msembe airstrip then a 45-60 minute drive; solar-powered. Banyan Group's first safari property and the second Banyan Tree Escape worldwide.
projects.impact: Ultra-premium branded supply in southern Tanzania's Ruaha circuit, a market of independent camps; expect rate-ceiling pressure on top-tier Ruaha camps.
projects.source: Banyan Group via Hospitality Net, 17 Sep 2026

projects.detail: All-suite hotel off Mombasa Road, 8km from JKIA and walking distance of the Nairobi SGR terminus: 112 one-bedroom, two-bedroom and presidential suites with kitchenettes and in-suite laundry; four meeting spaces totalling 623 m2 (largest 160-180 guests); rooftop pool and dining; complimentary 24-hour airport shuttle. The first voco in Kenya and East Africa.
projects.impact: Branded all-suite supply aimed squarely at the airport corridor's transit, crew and long-stay project nights. Independent airport-corridor hotels should expect voco's opening rates in Q4 corporate RFPs.

projects.detail: 84 rooms (45 doubles, 29 twins, six family, four accessible) at the highest point of the Ngorongoro Crater's eastern rim, 15 minutes from the crater gate; multimedia room for up to 40. Second property under Elewana's Explorer brand after Serengeti Explorer. Built on the site of a pre-existing property, so the operator says it adds no bed nights to the area.
projects.impact: A replacement, not an addition, on the rim — but it lands in the same 2027 season as the andBeyond Crater Lodge rebuild. Rim inventory is being repriced upward in 2027.
projects.source: Elewana announcement via Sleeper, 8 Sep 2026; Travel Daily News, Sep 2026

projects.detail: Closed to guests since 15 January 2025 for a complete rebuild, not a refurbishment. andBeyond put the reconstruction at roughly two years with a target re-opening of January 2027. The target date was announced in early 2024 and has not, as far as we can establish, been publicly re-confirmed since — treat January 2027 as an operator target rather than a fixed date.
projects.impact: This is a supply RETURN, not a supply addition, and it is the one most likely to be missed. One of the highest-rate properties on the northern circuit has been out of the market for two full seasons; its inventory comes back into a Ngorongoro crater-rim market that has repriced without it. If you sell the northern circuit, the 2027 high season is the one to model — rim demand that has been displaced to your property since 2025 has somewhere else to go the moment this reopens. Confirm the date directly with andBeyond before you build it into 2027 contracting.
projects.source: ARP Africa Travel trade notice (andBeyond announcement), March 2024; re-opening timing corroborated by Duma Explorer

projects.detail: Marriott's entry into Tanzania for the Autograph brand, signed with Catalonia Hotels & Resorts in Barcelona. New-build, all-inclusive, wellness-led: multiple pools, spa, theatre, oceanfront jetty with seawater pool.
projects.impact: The all-inclusive model is the thing to watch, not the room count. 271 all-inclusive keys on the Zanzibar north coast competes on total trip price, not nightly rate — beach properties selling room-only into the same European charter demand should expect their package comparison to get harder from 2027.

projects.detail: 181-key new-build on Zanzibar's northern coast: 37 suites, a presidential villa, 73 sea-view pool villas, plus branded apartments and penthouses. Six restaurants and bars.
projects.impact: Second major luxury brand signing on the same coastline for the same opening year. Two international luxury flags landing in 2027 within one stretch of northern Zanzibar means the premium beach segment there gets genuinely competitive — lock long-lead 2027 group and charter business earlier than usual.

projects.status: Phase 1 OPEN (2 of 5); 3 more planned for 2028
projects.opening: LUX* Lake Kivu (14 keys) and SALT of Akagera (60 keys) launched 15 June 2026; Volcanoes, Nyungwe and Akagera developments in 2028
projects.detail: Partnership with Cleo Capital Group for an ultra-luxury circuit across five sites. Phase 1 rebrands Cleo Lake Kivu as LUX* Lake Kivu and Akagera Game Lodge as SALT of Akagera. Phase 2 adds LUX* Volcanoes, LUX* Nyungwe and LUX* Akagera in 2028.
projects.impact: This is a circuit, not a hotel — it lets an operator sell Rwanda as a multi-night branded itinerary rather than a gorilla-permit stopover. Kenyan and Tanzanian bush operators should read it as Rwanda moving to capture more nights per trip from the same high-value guest.
projects.source: The Lux Collective press release, 15 June 2026 (read 5 Nov 2026); earlier The Lux Collective via Hospitality Net

projects.detail: 23-storey, 244-room property in Nakasero, central Kampala, on a management agreement with TWED Property Development Company. Hilton's entry into the Ugandan market.
projects.impact: First Hilton flag in Uganda. For Kampala city hotels the competitive question is corporate rate integrity — an international flag with a global corporate sales engine changes who wins the multinational and NGO account, more than it changes leisure demand.

projects.property: Kampala Marriott Hotel & Marriott Executive Apartments
projects.detail: 181 rooms and suites plus 96 serviced apartments on Nsambya Hill, Ggaba Road, Kampala; six restaurants, heated pool, spa. Opened by President Museveni on 27 Aug 2026. Owned by Capital Shoppers founders Ponsiano Ngabirano and family. Debuts both the Marriott Hotels and Marriott Executive Apartments brands in Uganda; Marriott now counts seven Ugandan properties across five brands.
projects.impact: Now open, alongside the Hilton Kampala project. 96 long-stay apartments compete directly for NGO, oil-and-gas and project-crew stays that Kampala serviced apartments and mid-scale hotels live on.
projects.source: Marriott International press release, 27 Aug 2026; Pulse Uganda, 27 Aug 2026

projects.property: Best Western Premier – Royal Golf View
projects.detail: 60 rooms plus 41 branded residences, two F&B outlets, health club and pool. Aleph Hospitality's third property in Kigali.
projects.impact: Mid-market, not luxury — and that matters. Kigali's branded supply is broadening beyond the top end, which is where conference and government per-diem business actually books.

projects.brand: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
projects.detail: Nine-suite property in Kigali's Rebero Hills, owned by Rwandan entrepreneur Sheila Kyarisiima. Joined SLH in 2026 — the brand's first Rwanda location. Private cinema, saltwater infinity pool, day-use spa and dining for post-safari guests before international flights.
projects.impact: Nine rooms will not move a market, but the SLH affiliation does: it puts Kigali on a global luxury booking platform. The day-use pre-flight model is also worth copying — it monetises the dead hours between a safari checkout and a night flight.
projects.source: SLH via Hospitality Net / Matador Network

projects.detail: Opened January 2026 near BK Arena and the 45,000-seat Amahoro Stadium, as part of the Kigali Sports City district.
projects.impact: Sports and events supply, deliberately sited. Rwanda is building hotel capacity around an events calendar rather than waiting for demand — the MICE and sports-tourism competition for regional conference business is getting sharper.

projects.property: La Maison Royale Westlands, South C and Masai Mara (to become Clarion x2 and Ascend Collection)
projects.status: In the Choice system, still trading as La Maison Royale; conversion to Clarion and Ascend not yet shown
projects.opening: Joined Choice in 2026 (bookable on choicehotels.com at 9 Nov 2026); Choice originally said 'early 2026'
projects.detail: CORRECTED 9 NOV 2026. Choice's own 4 Feb 2026 release names the three conversions: La Maison Royale Westlands (53 rooms) to become Clarion Hotel Westlands; La Maison Royale South C (59 rooms) to become Clarion Hotel South C; La Maison Royale Masai Mara (22 rooms), a safari lodge in the Olare Motorogi Conservancy, to join the Ascend Collection. Our earlier row, following Choice's 19 Nov 2025 release, listed a Clarion and a Quality Inn in the Nairobi CBD and placed the Mara property in the National Reserve. The Feb 2026 list has two Clarions and no Quality Inn, and the Mara lodge is in a conservancy, not the Reserve. At 9 Nov 2026 choicehotels.com lists all three, two of them bookable, under the La Maison Royale name with a 'New to Choice Hotels' label. None is yet shown under the Clarion or Ascend flag.
projects.impact: A soft-brand flag inside the Mara is the notable one. Ascend Collection lets an independent camp keep its identity while gaining US distribution — that is a direct competitive answer for Mara camps currently relying on OTA and agent volume, and a template other independents will follow.
projects.source: Choice Hotels EMEA release via Hospitality Net, 4 Feb 2026 (updated 20 Feb), hospitalitynet.org/news/4130739; Choice Hotels release, 19 Nov 2025 (media.choicehotels.com); choicehotels.com Kenya listings, read 9 Nov 2026

projects.property: Radisson Blu Hotel & Residence, Nairobi Arboretum
projects.opening: Autumn 2019 (Radisson release 3 Oct 2019; grand opening Feb 2020)
projects.detail: CORRECTED 9 NOV 2026. This row previously gave the opening as 2026. That was wrong: Radisson announced the opening on 3 October 2019. The hotel has 122 rooms and suites and was Radisson's third hotel in Kenya and its first extended-stay product in Nairobi, in Kilimani overlooking the Arboretum, next to State House. It has traded for six years and is not part of the 2026 pipeline. We keep the row only so that the correction is visible.
projects.impact: No new supply. This is existing upper-upscale stock in the Kilimani and Upper Hill corridor, and nothing about it should feed into a 2026–27 supply model.
projects.source: Radisson Hotel Group release, 3 Oct 2019 (via Le Journal des Palaces, pressrelease-56335); Business Traveller, 2 Oct 2019; The Star (KE), 4 Feb 2020 (grand opening)

projects.detail: Zanzibar authorities unveiled plans for what is described as East Africa's first seven-star hotel. Operator, room count, site and timeline are not confirmed.
projects.impact: Treat as a political and positioning signal, not a supply event — 'seven-star' is a marketing category, not a classification anyone awards. Worth tracking for what it says about Zanzibar's intent to move upmarket; worth nothing in a 2027 supply model until an operator and a site are named.

chains.note: Largest African pipeline of any operator.
Second by pipeline rooms (exact figure not published in the summary release).

data.caveat: W Hospitality Group notes that although more than 65,000 rooms are forecast to open across Africa in 2026 and 2027, historical actualisation rates suggest delivery will fall short of projection. Announced openings slip; treat every future-dated row here as an intention, not a delivery date.
